tools.description: Create a Cronping heartbeat monitor (dead-man's-switch). Returns a ping_url to call on each successful run of your agent loop, worker, or cron job, plus a claim_token to manage it. tools.name: ping_heartbeat
tools.description: Send a heartbeat signal to a Cronping check. signal="success" (default) marks it UP and resets the timer; "start" records that a run began (for duration); "fail" marks it DOWN immediately and alerts. tools.name: get_heartbeat_status
tools.description: Get the live status of a Cronping check (up/down/new, last ping time, ping count, and whether an alert channel is set).

tools.name: set_heartbeat_alert
tools.description: Add or change the alert channel on an EXISTING Cronping check (use this instead of creating a duplicate). Sets the email and/or webhook (Slack/Discord/generic https) that Cronping notifies when the monitor goes silent or recovers. Without an alert channel a check tracks status but can't warn you — c

tools.name: import_crontab
tools.description: Arm a dead-man's-switch for EVERY line of a crontab in one call. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: create_heartbeat, set_heartbeat_alert · Private data: ping_heartbeat · Public sink: create_heartbeat, ping_heartbeat, set_heartbeat_alert · Destructive: create_heartbeat, ping_heartbeat, import_crontab.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: create_heartbeat, set_heartbeat_alert · Private data: ping_heartbeat · Public sink: create_heartbeat, ping_heartbeat, set_heartbeat_alert · Destructive: create_heartbeat, ping_heartbeat, import_crontab

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
